papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric EEG state-derivative operator K and its spectral counterpart to extract time-odd, subject-discriminative longitudinal EEG features. Across four public datasets, polar orientation improved cross-session subject matching (e.g., Dortmund AUC 0.8901→0.9625, CMC@1 0.4757→0.6214), with fixed alpha-beta fusion reaching CMC@1=0.8350 and AUC=0.9855.

papers.title: Comparison of the Utility of Amplitude-Spectral and Coherence Features of Psychotropic Drugs' Action on ECoG Signal for Pharmaco-EEG Based Drug Screening in Rats.
papers.summary: Compared naive Bayesian classification of pharmaco-EEG data using amplitude-spectral features, coherence features, and their combination to identify psychoactive drug mechanisms in rats. Combined features correctly classified 20 of 24 test drug groups, while amplitude-spectral or coherence alone each classified 18 of 24; adding coherence significantly improved accuracy (p < 0.01).

papers.title: Diff-ADN: A diffusion-guided artifact denoising network with deterministic residual refinement for EEG.
papers.summary: The paper develops Diff-ADN, a two-stage diffusion-guided artifact denoising network with deterministic residual refinement for single-channel EEG artifact removal. It reports mean Pearson correlations of 0.936, 0.839, 0.886, and 0.844 for EOG, EMG, ECG, and mixed artifacts, respectively, and recovers 4.88–5.59 percentage points in motor-imagery decoding accuracy, with processing times of 12.52–17.08 ms per 2-s segment on CPU.

papers.title: Mu or alpha? Source decomposition for social perception analysis.
papers.summary: Compared sensor-level EEG with ICA-based source separation to assess whether central mu rhythm during emotional face perception is contaminated by visual alpha. ICA revealed distinct mu and alpha sources with opposite dynamics; mu showed synchronization and minimal sensitivity to facial expressions, suggesting prior mu suppression findings may reflect alpha contamination.

papers.title: Sleep electroencephalography-derived brain health and long-term cognitive decline in community-dwelling adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Tested whether sleep EEG-derived Brain Health Score (BHS) and Brain Age Index (BAI) predict future cognitive decline in 639 Framingham Heart Study participants followed for an average of 14.3 years. Each 1-SD higher BHS was associated with slower decline in memory, executive function, and language, whereas BAI was not associated with change in any cognitive domain.

papers.title: Attention Guided Conditional Adversarial Learning for EMG Artifact Suppression in Single Channel EEG
papers.summary: The paper evaluates P2P Trans, a conditional adversarial denoiser with attention-guided skip fusion, for EMG artifact suppression in single-channel EEG. It reports the best mean correlation coefficient of 0.8645 and lowest mean spectral RRMSE of 0.3596 against five convolutional encoder-decoder baselines, while noting a tradeoff in temporal waveform fidelity.

papers.title: Cross-variability decoding for motor imagery EEG signals: a comprehensive review.
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of cross-variability decoding methods for motor imagery EEG from 2020 to 2025. It critically evaluates deep learning and transfer learning approaches, including CNNs, transformers, feature alignment, domain adaptation, and meta-learning, across cross-subject and cross-session variability paradigms.

papers.title: Inter-rater reliability on rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns using Standardized Computer-based Organized Reporting of EEG (SCORE): A multicenter study.
papers.summary: Multicenter study assessed inter-rater reliability of rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns, background activity, and interictal findings using the SCORE framework across 10 EpiCARE centers. Overall RPP identification reached substantial agreement (κML .61–.66), individual RPP types almost perfect (κML up to .98), while posterior dominant rhythm reliability was low (κML .06–.47).

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for Alzheimer's disease characterization using small-sample EEG data.
papers.summary: This study evaluated an interpretable resting-state EEG framework using spectral and nonlinear complexity features from 63 participants (36 AD, 27 HC). Ridge Logistic regression achieved an exploratory AUC of 0.912 and accuracy of 0.857 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation; SHAP analysis highlighted posterior alpha activity, frontal and temporal theta power, and theta/alpha ratio, while microstate analysis revealed reduced Class B occurrence and increased Class C/D duration in AD.

papers.title: Conditional spatial classification of expert-confirmed interictal epileptiform discharge epochs: An EEG-ECG ablation and SHAP analysis.
papers.summary: Used 2,514 expert-confirmed 4-second interictal epileptiform discharge epochs to classify scalp distribution into five categories, testing channel ablations (19-channel EEG, EEG+ECG, full 29-channel). Linear discriminant analysis achieved 88.89% EEG-only accuracy, while CatBoost reached 93.25% with ECG and 94.44% with all channels; SHAP showed ECG channels contributed substantially and beta-band power was the top feature family.

papers.title: Reassessing Global Field Synchronization as a Phase-Synchrony EEG Metric: Mathematical Review and Empirical Counterexamples With Implications for Wearable Pain Monitoring.
papers.summary: Evaluated whether global field synchronization (GFS) validly represents EEG phase synchronization using synthetic simulations and empirical resting-state EEG. Simulations showed GFS was invariant to rotations that changed circular standard deviation and varied with scaling, while empirical data lacked a consistent inverse relationship between GFS and CSD across frequency bands, indicating GFS is not a valid proxy for phase synchronization.

papers.title: Pre-stimulus alpha power during mind-wandering in adults with ADHD.
papers.summary: EEG was recorded during a Go/No-Go task with thought probes in 28 medication-naïve adults with ADHD and 28 controls to characterize pre-stimulus alpha power dynamics during mind-wandering. Controls showed higher global alpha power without increased variability during mind-wandering, whereas ADHD patients exhibited no alpha power modulation between attentional states and higher alpha power variability during mind-wandering.

papers.title: EEG functional connectivity measures for differentiating 6-month consciousness-related outcome after brain injury.
papers.summary: In 111 patients with impaired consciousness after brain injury, the study explored whether EEG functional connectivity measures (wPLI, wPLI2, coherence) are associated with 6-month command-following outcome. Alpha-band wPLI during a moving condition showed a nominal group difference (p=0.006) but did not survive FDR correction (pFDR=0.169) and did not significantly improve discrimination beyond age and GCS (AUC 0.733 vs. 0.778 for clinical variables alone).

papers.title: Accent type modulates frequency-specific neural tracking of speech.
authors: Christina M Vanden Bosch der Nederlanden
papers.summary: Recorded EEG from Canadian English-speaking adults listening to Canadian (L1) and Mandarin-accented (L2) English in quiet conditions and measured neural tracking via speech-envelope coherence. Found significantly stronger neural tracking for L1-accented speech in delta-theta and higher-frequency bands, with transcription errors correlating with neural tracking.

papers.title: N,N-Dimethyltryptamine and harmine formulation alters transient EEG topography sequences near the peak of the psychedelic state.
papers.summary: In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled EEG study with 25 participants, the effects of an ayahuasca-inspired DMT/harmine formulation on EEG microstate dynamics were compared to harmine alone and placebo. DMT/harmine was associated with reduced microstate duration, increased occurrence and complexity, and less random transition sequences, consistent with increased metastability and signal diversity.

papers.title: Effects of lidocaine bolus and infusion on neuromonitoring by bispectral index (BIS®), electroencephalogram periodic and aperiodic activity, and Surgical Pleth Index® during propofol-remifentanil anaesthesia: a single-centre prospective observational study.
papers.summary: Observational study in 20 female patients under stable propofol-remifentanil anaesthesia assessed dose-dependent effects of lidocaine bolus and infusion on EEG spectral features and processed parameters. Lidocaine increased delta and decreased beta activity, reduced alpha peak bandwidth and center frequency, and altered aperiodic slope earlier than changes in BIS, SEF95, and SPI.

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Electroencephalography Predicts Acute Cerebral Injury in the Pediatric ICU.
papers.summary: This prospective study applied multiple machine learning classifiers to clinical and EEG background features to predict acute cerebral injury in 201 pediatric ICU patients. The support vector machine with radial basis function kernel achieved the highest accuracy for binary injury detection (AUROC 0.95, test accuracy 0.90), while logistic regression performed best for multiclass unilateral versus bilateral injury classification (test accuracy 0.77).

papers.title: Acute administration of methylphenidate modulates functional connectivity during irrelevant stimuli processing in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over trial examined acute methylphenidate (20 mg) effects on event-related EEG functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease patients during a visual oddball task. Compared to placebo, methylphenidate decreased theta-band functional connectivity and global efficiency in fronto-parietal networks during processing of task-irrelevant standard stimuli.

papers.title: Preparation of Acute Mouse Hippocampal Brain Sections for Transport to a Distant Electrophysiology Laboratory.
papers.summary: The paper describes a standardized protocol for preparing and transporting acute mouse hippocampal slices to distant electrophysiology laboratories, emphasizing viability preservation during transport via sucrose-based protective solutions, controlled rewarming, and oxygenated aCSF in sealed containers. Validation with patch-clamp recordings showed that electrophysiological properties, including resting membrane potential, input resistance, action potential firing, and spontaneous synaptic neurotransmission, remained comparable to freshly prepared slices.

papers.title: Age-related cortical mechanisms underlying postural control: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 37 studies (1,302 participants) characterized age-related alterations in cortical activity during standing balance tasks with sensory, cognitive, and mechanical challenges. The evidence indicated that older adults show diminished task-dependent cortical modulation, weaker associations between cortical activity and postural sway, and delayed sensorimotor processing during challenging balance tasks compared to younger adults.

papers.title: Multi-modal connectome analysis of the stereoelectroencephalography implantation effect: a case report.
papers.summary: In a single case of drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, longitudinal multimodal connectome analysis showed that SEEG implantation was associated with decreased hippocampus-amygdala and fusiform-temporal pole connectivity, increased hippocampus-posterior cingulate connectivity, and reduced connectome gradient eccentricity (11.9% after SEEG, 17.6% after lobectomy), alongside lymphocytic infiltration and reactive gliosis around electrode trajectories.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machine and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states using resting-state EEG features, including spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved the highest performance with 96.88% accuracy at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Temporal EEG coupling during precuneus low-frequency rTMS in drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.summary: No abstract was provided, so the study's methods and results cannot be summarized.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG biomarkers of general and domain-specific cognitive impairment and plasma P-tau217 in patients with Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: This study examined resting-state quantitative EEG biomarkers in 360 participants (AD dementia, MCI, and healthy controls) for detecting cognitive impairment and associations with plasma P-tau217. EEG achieved AUCs of 0.70–0.87 for distinguishing AD-related cognitive dysfunction, and right parietal relative power was negatively correlated with and an independent factor for increased plasma P-tau217 (AUC 0.68).

papers.title: Clinical and preclinical investigation of the mechanism promoting aura in post-traumatic headache and inhibition of pain-related behavior in mice by onabotulinumtoxinA.
papers.summary: In humans, 32% of patients with post-traumatic headache developed new-onset aura, and in a mouse model of mTBI, injured mice showed a 160% increase in cortical spreading depression (CSD) induction probability; onabotulinumtoxinA did not alter CSD susceptibility but completely abolished optogenetic CSD-induced allodynia.

papers.title: EEG reveals what the eyes can't see: A clinical vignette of epileptic visual loss.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: A clinical vignette describes a case of epileptic visual loss in which EEG revealed seizures despite the patient's inability to see. The case highlights the diagnostic role of EEG in identifying occult ictal activity underlying visual loss.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations in Anhedonia Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder and Their Modulation by Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation.
papers.summary: The study stratified 50 MDD patients into high- and low-anhedonia groups and assessed EEG microstate dynamics before and after 2 weeks of intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS). High-anhedonia patients showed persistent microstate abnormalities after iTBS, while low-anhedonia patients largely normalized, suggesting subtype-specific neuromodulation effects and a potential treatment response marker.

papers.title: Understanding the impact of perceived emotional valence of eco-labels for novel food products on consumer preferences, visual attention, and cognition - a multimodal study using EEG and eye tracking.
papers.summary: This multimodal EEG and eye-tracking study found that eco-labels with high perceived positivity increased purchase intentions, were associated with shorter fixation durations and fewer fixations, and modulated P300 and LPP amplitudes; higher P300 increased purchase intentions while greater N200 reduced them for high-positivity labels.

papers.title: Case Report: Seizure freedom after resection of a temporal choroidal fissure cyst in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.summary: A 35-year-old woman with drug-resistant epilepsy and a right temporal choroidal fissure cyst achieved seizure freedom (Engel Class IA/ILAE Class 1) after SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation followed by anterior temporal lobectomy; SEEG and intraoperative ECoG confirmed an epileptogenic focus adjacent to the cyst, with no histopathological evidence of hippocampal sclerosis or focal cortical dysplasia.

papers.title: Neural Dynamics of Self-Control: Pre-Choice EEG Signals Predict Yielding to Temptation
papers.summary: Introduced a dynamometer-based task in which 26 participants chose between high-effort/larger-later and low-effort/smaller-sooner rewards during 32-channel EEG, producing frequent switching toward smaller-sooner options in temptation trials. Pre-choice late positive potential differentiated stay from switch trials, and multivariate decoding discriminated outcomes 304–348 ms post-option presentation via frontal and centroparietal networks, indicating that neural bias toward yielding is established before the initial choice and reflects reward anticipation rather than self-control signals.

papers.title: High-Density Spectral Analysis for Bi-Atrial Arrhythmogenic Substrate During Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: High-density CARTOFINDER mapping in 47 non-paroxysmal AF patients showed that both focal and rotational activation sites exhibited higher dominant frequency deviation (DFD) and regularity index (RI) than non-focal/non-rotational sites, with the left atrium demonstrating higher DFD and RI than the right atrium. High-repetition rotational sites had higher RI but paradoxically lower DFD compared to low-repetition sites.

papers.title: Bilateral Angular Gyrus 810-nm Transcranial Near-Infrared Stimulation Reshapes Brain Network: Ameliorate Alzheimer's Disease Cognitive Deficits.
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled trial of 36 biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease patients, targeted 810-nm transcranial near-infrared stimulation over the bilateral angular gyrus improved cognition, memory, language, attention, and executive functions while reducing neuropsychiatric symptoms. fMRI showed enhanced default mode network connectivity and functional synergy with dorsal attention, frontoparietal, and limbic networks, and TMS-EEG demonstrated enhanced information flow and prefrontal/temporo-occipital activation.

papers.title: Delayed late ventricular depolarization is associated with inflammation in epicardial Fat Among females: a New avenue in cardiac electrophysiology.
papers.summary: In 146 cardiac surgery patients, epicardial adipose tissue inflammatory and fibrotic markers correlated with delayed late anteroseptal depolarization (prolonged S-wave upstroke time) in females but not males, with linear regression confirming sex-specific associations for CD14, CD16, DEFA3, and COL1A2. Findings suggest that ECG can indicate adverse epicardial adipose tissue phenotypes in a sex-dependent manner.

papers.title: Effectiveness and multidimensional mechanisms of close-to-bone needling in knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: Randomized controlled trial in 70 knee osteoarthritis patients found that close-to-bone needling (CBN) produced greater improvements in WOMAC, ISOA, and SF-36 scores, greater reductions in cartilage degeneration, synovial thickening, and joint effusion, and stronger modulation of miR-140, miR-30, IL-1β, and TNF-α compared to celecoxib. EEG analysis revealed reduced Delta/Theta power, increased Alpha/Beta/Gamma power in frontoparietal regions, and normalization of prefrontal connectivity in CBN group.

papers.title: Pediatric MOGAD in the Intensive Care Unit: A Case Series.
papers.summary: Retrospective review of 124 pediatric MOGAD patients identified 37 requiring ICU admission for altered mental status, seizures, or weakness; 16 were intubated, 18 had seizures, and 12 had neuroimaging evidence of increased intracranial pressure. The study characterizes severe MOGAD presentations but found no specific EEG biomarkers for MOGAD.

papers.title: A rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication with tetrasomy (CN=4) and adjacent trisomy (CN=3) associated with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a Chinese girl with a de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication comprising a ~10.34 Mb tetrasomic segment and an adjacent ~2.40 Mb trisomic segment, presenting with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, profound cognitive and language impairment, delayed myelination, and subclinical epileptiform discharges. The findings expand the genomic spectrum of complex proximal 15q rearrangements and highlight the value of high-resolution genomic testing.

papers.title: Modulation of immune responses by acupuncture at Jing-Well points in neurological disorders: exploring mechanisms and clinical applications in the era of modern electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on acupuncture at Jing-Well points for modulating immune responses in neurological disorders, focusing on neuroimmune, electrophysiological, and clinical aspects. It reports that direct evidence for Jing-Well point stimulation is limited, but broader acupuncture research suggests anti-inflammatory, autonomic, and neuroprotective effects, highlighting the need for standardized studies.

papers.title: Hirschsprung's disease and a rare mutation of the PIGO gene: Mabry syndrome.
papers.summary: Case report of a 2-year-old Turkish boy with Mabry syndrome (HPMRS2) due to a novel homozygous PIGO p.Arg445Pro variant, presenting with neurodevelopmental delay, seizures, hyperphosphatasia, and Hirschsprung's disease. Rectal biopsy confirmed aganglionosis; after definitive surgery, spontaneous defecation was achieved except for rare enterocolitis episodes.

papers.title: Hemimegalencephaly with accelerated myelination in the affected hemisphere.
papers.summary: Case report of a 7-month-old boy with left hemimegalencephaly presenting with neonatal-onset seizures and developmental delay. Brain MRI showed hemispheric enlargement, dysmorphic gyri, an aberrant midsagittal fiber tract, and accelerated myelination in the affected hemisphere, illustrating a recognizable imaging pattern for early diagnosis.

papers.title: Electrophysiology procedures for preventing falls in older people living in the community.
papers.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
papers.summary: This is a protocol for a Cochrane systematic review that will assess the efficacy and safety of electrophysiology procedures in preventing falls among older people living in the community. No results are reported.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
